festivals.name: Sabine Parish Fair & Rodeo
festivals.tagline: Fair days. Rodeo nights. Hometown memories.
festivals.description: Meet at the midway for four days of rides, livestock shows, hometown talent, and evenings at the arena. The Sabine Festival & Rodeo brings Many together for a fall tradition shared across generations.
festivals.address: Sabine Parish Fairgrounds · 115 Fairgrounds Road, Many, LA 71449
festivals.source_note: Schedule transcribed from the supplied 2026 Sabine Festival & Rodeo flyer. Gate prices refer to the stated entry windows; rides and rodeo may have separate charges. The organizer website still displays a 2025 program. Confirm changes with the organizers.

information.title: A fair with a theme
information.body: The 2026 theme is “Red, White, Blue Ribbons: Celebrating America’s Best.” Look for community exhibits, youth livestock events, and four evenings of midway fun.

information.title: Plan your visit
information.body:
The main fair runs September 23–26 at the Sabine Parish Fairgrounds in Many. Barrel racing takes place at the Benton Johnson Rodeo Arena on the same grounds. The parade lines up at St. Joseph Church in Many at noon on Saturday.

Gate admission is free Wednesday evening and during Friday’s 9 AM–3 PM educational program. The flyer lists $5 gate entry Thursday, Friday, and Saturday from 6–10 PM. Rodeo tickets, carnival rides, and food may cost extra; the flyer does not give those prices.

information.title: Entering an exhibit?
information.body:
Arts, crafts, and 4-H entries are accepted September 18 from 3:30–5:45 PM and September 19 from 9–11 AM in the Exhibit Building. Those windows also cover decorating 4-H Club bulletin boards. Judging on September 20–21 is closed to the public.

Use the lead-up days switch on the calendar to see entry windows and Monday barrel racing.

information.title: About the film
information.body: The Fair Comes Alive is a 30-second creative promo made by SatCom, combining local footage with AI-assisted scenes and music. It is a visual celebration of the fair, not a recording of the upcoming 2026 event.

festivals.name: Zwolle Tamale Fiesta
festivals.tagline: A little town. A whole lot of flavor.
festivals.description: Follow the music to Zwolle for the 50th annual Tamale Fiesta. Three days of tamales, dancing, a hometown parade, and anniversary fireworks make room for old friends and new faces.
festivals.address: Zwolle Festival Grounds · 1100 S. Main St., Zwolle, LA 71486
festivals.source_note: Dates, activities, and gate prices checked against the organizer’s published 2026 program on September 15. The daily program supports October 8–10; its footer has an inconsistent October 8–11 range. Race start times and the tamale eating contest time differ within the published materials. Confirm these with organizers.

information.title: Fifty years of coming together
information.body: The Fiesta began with an idea proposed by Rogers P. Loupe in 1975. With help from tourism director Roscoe Carruth, it developed into a nonprofit celebration of Zwolle’s food and Spanish and Indigenous heritage. In 2026, the festival marks its 50th annual gathering.

information.title: Plan your visit
information.body:
Public gates open at 4 PM Thursday and Friday, and 8 AM Saturday. Gate admission is $2 Thursday, $5 Friday, and $10 Saturday. Food, rides, and some activities cost extra. Ask the organizers about child admission, parking, accessibility, and accepted payment methods.

Saturday’s mud bog begins at 2 PM. Its published $25 cooler charge and $40 tent-space charge apply specifically to the mud-bog area; they do not establish festival-wide cooler permission.

information.title: Run, walk & join the parade crowd
information.body:
The program lists Saturday race registration at 7 AM and a 5K start at 8 AM. A separate registration listing gives a different start time, so confirm with organizers. Both the 5K and one-mile entry are listed at $25; the first 75 paid participants are listed as eligible for shirts.

The 5K registration deadline is September 28 at 11:59 PM Central; the one-mile deadline is October 1 at 11:59 PM Central. The parade begins at 10 AM Saturday.

information.title: Vendors, sponsors & the pageant
information.body:
The organizer reports food and arts-and-crafts spaces as fully booked. Contact the festival for availability changes. The 2026 pageant was held August 22 and is a past event.

Sponsorship levels start at $150, with the published sponsorship deadline of October 1. General questions and sponsorship inquiries can go to Chris and Becky Loupe at the email below.

festivals.name: Sabine Freestate Festival
festivals.tagline: Western history, smoky BBQ, and a weekend in Florien.
festivals.description: Florien’s 46th annual Sabine Freestate Festival brings together western reenactments, a parade, live music and the No Man’s Land BBQ Championship. Explore three days of community events, with pageant and clue dates leading up to the weekend.
festivals.address: Florien, Louisiana · Activities at several local venues; see the schedule
festivals.source_note: Schedule transcribed from the organizer’s 2026 festival flyer supplied by the site owner. The official Sabine Freestate Festival website confirms the 46th annual 2026 event and lists the organizer email and contact address. Descriptions are independently written. Admission, most activity locations and lead-up times are not listed on the flyer; check with organizers for those details and schedule changes.

information.title: A weekend in Florien
information.body:
The festival runs November 6–8, 2026. Friday and Saturday list an 11 PM grounds closing time. Sunday’s final advertised activity is movie night at 6 PM; the movie is still to be announced.

The flyer does not give gate admission or individual activity prices. Ask the organizers about parking, accessibility and exact locations before traveling.

information.title: No Man’s Land BBQ Championship
information.body: The entry deadline is November 5; no deadline time is printed. Head cooks meet November 6 at 5:30 PM at the Train Depot. Saturday’s turn-in is at 5 PM, with champions announced at 6:45 PM. Email the organizers for entry requirements and fees.

information.title: Saturday with the family
information.body: The parade starts at 11 AM. Dog shows, dance, stockyard activities and evening bands fill out Saturday’s program. Roller car rides, laser tag, minnow racing, putt-putt, historical demonstrations, Chuckwagon Will Travel and LA Mechanical Bulls are also listed throughout the day.

information.title: History & the clue trail
information.body: The festival commemorates the area known as No Man’s Land between 1806 and 1821. Staged western shootouts are scheduled all three festival days. The flyer lists ten numbered clues, beginning October 17; rules and prizes are not specified.

information.title: Contact the organizers
information.body: Email sabineparishfreestate@gmail.com for entries, visitor questions or updates. The official website lists the contact address as 220 W Port Arthur Ave, Florien, LA 71429. This is the organizer’s contact address; individual activities use the venues shown in the schedule.
